meta.title: "That's not what I said" — the phrase that pulls a conversation back to your child's actual words | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child one phrase that takes their words back when someone stretches them to an extreme. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: Does your child go quiet when their words get twisted?
hero.subheadline: Not because they can't defend an idea. They just don't have a simple tool to bring the conversation back to what they actually said.

media.alt: A child going quiet when their words get twisted

pain.title: The straw man: when someone argues with a made-up version of your words, not with you
pain.body:
"I don't want to go today" → "so nothing is ever good enough for you". "This is hard for me" → "so you just don't want to try". Your child says one thing — and gets answered on something else entirely. They feel it's unfair, but can't name it: "that's not what I said" gets stuck in their throat.

This isn't a child who explains poorly or lacks confidence. It's a technique — their idea gets stretched to an extreme ("always", "everything", "never") so it's easier to knock down. Now they're arguing against a version they never voiced. In that game they always lose: the other side's version of their words sounds so harsh that agreeing feels impossible, and disproving it is hard.

The result — the child either starts justifying themselves (and steps into someone else's game) or shuts down. Either way, their real point disappears from the conversation.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
